'''David A. Steen''' is an American [[herpetologist]] and [[conservation biology|conservation biologist]].<ref name=steen/> He is Reptile and Amphibian Research Leader of the Fish and Wildlife Research Institute (Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission), and was previously a research professor at [[Auburn University]], where he completed his Ph.D.<ref name=tftt2017/><ref name=steen/> Steen runs a popular [[Twitter]] account where he offers reptile and amphibian identification and dispels myths about oft-maligned snakes such as [[Agkistrodon contortrix|copperhead]]s, [[cottonmouth]]s, and [[rattlesnake]]s.<ref name=lund2015/><ref name=awtwit/><ref name=wootson2018/>

He won the Mindlin Foundation's "Mindlin Science Communication Prize" in 2017 for his efforts in online [[science communication]].<ref name=mindwin/><ref name=mindabt/> He is author of the book Secrets of Snakes: the Science Beyond the Myths.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Steen |first1=David A. |title=Secrets of Snakes: the Science Beyond the Myths |date=2019 |publisher=Texas A&M University Press |isbn=978-1-62349-797-2 |pages=184 |edition=First}}</ref>

In 2018, along with researchers Sean P. Graham, Richard Kline, and Crystal Kelehear, he described a new species of aquatic [[salamander]] [[endemic]] to the [[Gulf Coastal Plain]], ''[[Siren reticulata]]'', known as the reticulated siren or leopard eel.<ref name=graham2018/><ref name=bittel2018/><ref name=wildsiren2018/>
